subject: How to constrain each element of an array with a sum of elements of other arrays

messages.author: 83b63066408210ec
messages.subject: How to constrain each element of an array with a sum of elements of other arrays
parts:
Suppose I have a model with these data and parametres:

data {
    int <lower = 1> n_elements_1;
    int <lower = 1> n_elements_2;
    int <lower = 1> n_elements_3;
    
    ...
}

parameters {
    real A [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];
    real B [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];
    real <upper = A + B> C [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];
    
    ...
}

...

What I want with that upper bound is to ensure that C [i, j, k] <= A [i, j, k] + B [i, j, k] for all i, j, k, but the above doesn't work, and the error it gives me is that it can't add real [,,] + real [,,]. Is there a way to do it?

messages.author: b1e64236b865525c
messages.subject: Re: How to constrain each element of an array with a sum of elements of other arrays
parts: As per the answer you got from Ben Goodrich yesterday, I suppose one way you could do it is:

parameters {
    real A [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];
    real B [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];

real <upper = 1> scale [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];
}
transformed parameters {
    real C [n_elements_1, n_elements_2, n_elements_3];
    for (i in 1: n_elements_1) {
        for (j in 1: n_elements_2) {
            for (k in 1: n_elements_3) {
                C [i, j, k] = scale [i, j, k] * (A [i, j, k] + B [i, j, k]);
            }
        }
    }
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: How to constrain each element of an array with a sum of elements of other arrays
parts:
Not yet for whole arrays of constraints.

You'll have to do the transform yourself and you'll
need to take care of the Jacobian if it's something
you want to give a distribution with a sampling statement.

- Bob
